name: Relfydess

card.summary: Galderma's ready-to-use liquid botulinum toxin for frown lines, supported by a Phase 3 trial.
card.note: Prescription-only injectable; limited independent literature so far.

quick.overview:
Relfydess is a liquid botulinum toxin A from Galderma that needs no reconstitution. It is aimed at frown lines.

Its Phase 3 READY-1 trial compared it with placebo in adults with moderate-to-severe glabellar lines.
quick.mechanism: Like other type A toxins, it weakens injected muscles by blocking nerve signals to them.
quick.risks: It is a prescription injectable. Trial safety findings were not reviewed here, and off-label uses appear only as case reports.

lead: Relfydess (relabotulinumtoxinA) is a ready-to-use liquid botulinum toxin type A made by Galderma. It is injected by a clinician into facial muscles to relax them, which smooths dynamic wrinkles such as the frown lines between the eyebrows (glabellar lines) and the crow's feet at the corners of the eyes (lateral canthal lines). Its main difference from older products is that it arrives as a liquid and does not need to be reconstituted from powder.[1][2]

It is manufactured with Galderma's PEARL technology, which the company's authors describe as producing a potent, complex-free formulation.[2] In the Phase 3 READY-1 trial of adults with moderate-to-severe glabellar lines, 297 participants were randomized 3 to 1 to relabotulinumtoxinA or placebo over six months, with the month-1 composite responder rate of 82.9 percent in the treated group in the abstract.[2] Patient-reported outcomes from the same trial showed 97.7 percent of treated participants reporting at least one grade of improvement at month 1, falling to 71.0 percent at month 6.[3]

A second Phase 3 study, READY-2, tested the product in lateral canthal lines, and a 2026 case report describes off-label use for Frey's syndrome.[4][5] Botulinum toxins as a class are prescription-only injectables.

chain: Injected into frown and eye-corner muscles
Dynamic lines soften and the brow area looks smoother
angle.text: Relfydess is used to soften frown lines and crow's feet by temporarily relaxing the muscles that crease the skin. Trials report effects within days that fade over several months.

paras: The product is presented as a liquid toxin that is ready to inject, made through PEARL technology (precipitation-free extraction and activity-preserving refined liquid) from a proprietary Clostridium botulinum type A1 strain.[2][6] Most botulinum toxin products for aesthetic use must be reconstituted before use; ready-to-use liquids are a more recent development, and a 2026 review lists relabotulinumtoxinA and abobotulinumtoxinA (Alluscience) among them.[1][6] The same review places relabotulinumtoxinA with incobotulinumtoxinA and daxibotulinumtoxinA as complex-free toxins, and notes that drug stabilisers differ across products.[1]

Like other type A toxins, it weakens injected muscles by blocking nerve signals to them, using the SNAP-25 cleavage pathway.[6] In laboratory work, specific bioactivity of relabotulinumtoxinA was compared with powder onabotulinumtoxinA using binding, internalization and SNAP-25 cleavage assays.[6] A 2026 comparison of three complex-free toxins found comparable relative bioactivity per labeled unit between incobotulinumtoxinA, daxibotulinumtoxinA and relabotulinumtoxinA in vitro.[7]

Adults with moderate-to-severe glabellar lines were randomized 3:1 to relabotulinumtoxinA or placebo in a six-month, double-blind, multicenter Phase 3 study. The primary endpoint was a composite of at least two grades of improvement on investigator and participant scales at month 1 at maximum frown.[2] Patient-reported results published in 2025 in Aesthetic Surgery Journal covered 233 treated adults and 74 placebo participants, with at least one grade of improvement on the participant scale in 97.2 percent at day 7, 97.7 percent at month 1, 90.0 percent at month 3 and 71.0 percent at month 6, versus 18.9 to 27.5 percent with placebo; satisfaction and well-being questionnaires were also used.[3]

In READY-2, 230 adults received relabotulinumtoxinA and 73 placebo. The month-1 composite two-grade responder rate was 51.8 percent versus 1.4 percent, and 87.2 percent of treated participants were rated none or mild versus 11.9 percent. Onset was reported by day 1 in 34 percent, median return to baseline severity was 24.7 weeks, and mild to moderate treatment-related adverse events occurred in a minority of participants.[4]
A 2026 case report described a 72-year-old man treated off-label with intradermal injections for gustatory sweating and flushing after parotidectomy and radiotherapy.[5]

The READY-2 abstract reports mild to moderate treatment-related adverse events in 6.1 percent of treated participants.[4] The READY-1 trial reported treatment-emergent adverse events as a secondary outcome.[2] Botulinum toxins as a class are prescription-only and administered by clinicians.

timeline.event: READY-1 Phase 3 efficacy and safety results published in Aesthetic Surgery Journal.[2]
Patient-reported READY-1 outcomes and READY-2 lateral canthal line results published.[3][4]
Case report of off-label use for Frey's syndrome published.[5]
